paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The difference between probing a single layer and probing the weighted sum of layers. concat is the concatenation of all layers. 0 is the embedding layer. Large negative values on the y-axis mean that probing the particular layer on the x-axis is much worse than probing the weighted sum of all layers.
model_annotation: The figure consists of two vertically stacked bar charts that illustrate the difference between probing a single layer and probing the weighted sum of layers for two models, "mBERT" (top subplot) and "XLM-R" (bottom subplot). In both charts, the horizontal axis contains the categories, ordered sequentially by layer number from 0 to 12, followed by a final category named "concat"; the bottom chart explicitly labels this axis as "layer". The vertical axis for both charts is a linear scale labeled "% point difference," with a visible range extending from slightly below -10 to slightly above 0, featuring numeric tick labels at intervals of 2 from -10 to 0, accompanied by corresponding horizontal grid lines. The top chart represents the mBERT model using light blue bars with black outlines. These bars exhibit a general trend of decreasing negative magnitude from left to right across the early layers, starting from the most negative value of approximately -10.5 at layer 0 and rising toward zero. Layers 9, 10, and "concat" show slight positive values, with "concat" reaching a maximum positive value of approximately 0.4, while layer 12 drops back to roughly -1.2. The bottom chart represents the XLM-R model using dark blue bars with black outlines. Similar to the top chart, the early layers display large negative values, with layers 0 and 1 being the most negative at approximately -9.5. The bar values gradually approach zero up to layer 9 (roughly -0.3), transition to small positive values at layers 10, 11, and "concat" (all near 0.4), and show a minor negative dip at layer 12 (approximately -0.2). In both subplots, the bars are sorted categorically by the sequential order of the model layers and the final concatenated representation, rather than by value, and no specific bars are uniquely emphasized beyond their uniform colored fills and borders.
